new_entities.name: Kisspeptin in hypogonadotropic hypogonadism
aliases: kisspeptin challenge in idiopathic hypogonadotropic hypogonadism
new_entities.description: Use of exogenous kisspeptin as a physiologic probe or potential restorative therapy in congenital or idiopathic hypogonadotropic hypogonadism.

new_entities.name: Testosterone recovery
new_entities.description: Recovery or normalization of serum testosterone levels in hypogonadal men.

edges.effect_quant: Kisspeptin has not shown reliable testosterone restoration in established congenital or idiopathic hypogonadotropic hypogonadism, but selected reversal phenotypes can display physiologic responsiveness. In a seven-patient IHH case series, no participant responded to exogenous kisspeptin and sex-steroid treatment did not restore responsiveness, whereas a six-man reversal cohort showed kisspeptin-induced LH pulses only in those with sustained endogenous reversal; a 21-man congenital HH study likewise found a markedly blunted LH rise after kisspeptin-54 versus healthy controls.
edges.population: men with congenital or idiopathic hypogonadotropic hypogonadism, including reversal phenotypes and classic persistent disease
edges.mechanism: Kisspeptin acts upstream of GnRH neurons, so efficacy depends on whether the hypothalamic GnRH network is functionally present and capable of responding; that appears absent in many established congenital HH cases but partly recoverable in reversal states.
edges.summary: This is a mixed and still exploratory edge. Kisspeptin is biologically important to the reproductive axis, but as a practical route to testosterone recovery in hypogonadotropic hypogonadism it remains inconsistent and phenotype-dependent rather than reliably therapeutic.
edges.caveats: Most human studies are small physiologic challenge studies that measure LH responsiveness rather than durable testosterone recovery over time. The signal is best interpreted as a probe of residual hypothalamic function, not a proven replacement strategy.

evidence.citation: Lippincott MF et al 2016 J Clin Endocrinol Metab
evidence.notes: Kisspeptin Responsiveness Signals Emergence of Reproductive Endocrine Activity: Implications for Human Puberty.
